data.hypothesis: With block and items_per_block held at 256, a 768-source tile may reduce shared-memory staging and synchronization rounds relative to the 512 tile while using less shared memory than the 1024 tile. Its 12,288 bytes of static shared memory fit the 49,152-byte limit; the timing effect remains for controller evaluation.
data.notes: Launch settings remain block=256, items_per_block=256, shared_memory_bytes=0. The four static arrays use 4 × 768 × sizeof(float) = 12,288 bytes. This candidate is unmeasured; supplied results show 256/512 slightly ahead of 256/256 and 256/1024 lower, but do not establish the performance of 256/768.
transformations: Change SOURCE_TILE_SIZE from 256 to 768, keeping one thread per target, the existing force arithmetic and self-interaction exclusion, and the 256-thread launch geometry.
